neighbours.label: the spelling unit 'fit' as a whole-word adjective or name piece (fit to play, unfit, Fitton), and the same sound in phyto-/fito- plant words
fire: The doctors declared the striker fit for the final on Sunday.
The inspector found the old building unfit for human use.
These berries are rich in phytochemicals that may protect the heart.
Sir James Fitton served as a judge in Dublin for many years.
Los agricultores aplican productos fitosanitarios antes de la cosecha.
Both of the defenders should be fit to start this weekend.
The judge called the father unfit to care for his children.
Many teas contain phytoestrogens and other plant compounds.
quiet: The doctors declared the striker healthy for the final on Sunday.
The inspector found the old building empty for many years.
These berries are rich in sugars that may spoil the jam.
Sir James Walton served as a judge in Dublin for many years.
Los agricultores venden productos frescos antes de la cosecha.
These jeans fit me better than the ones I bought last week.
The judge called the father late to the hearing for his children.
Many teas contain caffeine and other natural flavors.

notes: Card: ' fit' x11, 'to' x6 after phy-, ' unfit' x5, ' Fit' x3, 'yt', 'ton'. Probes: 'fit to play' 0.887, 'to' in Phytochemicals 0.843, Fitton 0.727, fitosanitarios 0.710, unfit 0.684; 'ready to play' 0.002, 'Vegetables' 0.005, and the verb in 'The shoes fit well' only 0.032. So the verb is a near miss. Whether it is one spelling unit or two is open; the declared trigger counts only the fit tokens.
